<!-- Generated by @afokapu/atdd-linear {{VERSION}}. Do not edit; run `atdd-linear agent init --replace`. -->

The repository's `plan/` decides what exists and what it means; Linear decides who works on it and when. `atdd-linear` projects one into the other, configured by `atdd-linear.yaml` (the team key, the mirrored documents, the cycle names). The package README in `node_modules/@afokapu/atdd-linear/` has the details; do not restate it.

## What each level means

| Level | Answers | Named | Who makes it |
|---|---|---|---|
| Initiative | Who or what is it for? | a customer, programme or outcome | people |
| Project | What are we building? | `<TEAM KEY>: <scope>`, e.g. `FOS: First playable` | people; `release` writes its summary and description |
| Milestone | Which journey? | `<order> · <journey title>`, with `journey:<id>` in its description | people; `release` writes the journey |
| Cycle | When did it ship? | the version, from `cycles:` in `atdd-linear.yaml` | Linear; `sync` names it and writes its release notes |
| Issue | a feature | from the plan | `sync` |
| Sub-issue | a WMBT, its acceptances as checkboxes | from the plan | `sync`; Done only when its tests pass |
| `wagon` / `train:` labels, `Train ·` / `Journey ·` views | wagon, interlocking, journey | from the plan | `sync` |

A version is a cycle, never a project: a project is a scope that ships across as many cycles as it takes. Do not make a project per version, or views per release (the project page already groups by milestone).

## Who owns what

The repository owns, and every sync overwrites: titles, the part of a description above the ✍️ notes marker, the parent, the `wagon` and `train:` labels, whether a WMBT is Done, the mirrored documents, the release notes above their marker, and the names of cycles that had none. To change any of these, change `plan/` or the docs and let the sync run; an edit made in Linear is lost on the next sync.

People own, and the sync never touches: initiatives, projects, milestones, which cycle an issue is in, assignee, priority, estimate, comments, other labels, and anything below the notes marker. Change these only when the user asks.

Never edit or remove an issue's `atdd-urn:` line: it is how the sync finds the issue again.

## Commands

- `bunx atdd-linear sync` prints what would change and changes nothing. Run it first, and read the plan of changes.
- `sync --apply` belongs to CI, on every merge to main, with `--results` from the test run. Do not run it locally without `--results <junit.xml>`: tests decide Done in both directions, so a run with no results reopens every Done WMBT and corrupts the release notes. A run from a feature branch writes that branch's plan, not main's.
- `bunx atdd-linear release "<project name>" [--apply]` after people create a project or add, rename or reorder its milestones. Safe to run locally.
- `--scope <interlocking>` on `sync` previews a slice; a scoped run never cancels anything.

## Never

- Delete anything in Linear. Something removed from the plan is cancelled by the sync with a comment; deleting is the user's to do.
- Add "blocked by" relations. Order lives in the plan's continuations and in milestone order.
- Print, paste or log the API key. It comes from `LINEAR_API_KEY`, or on macOS from the Keychain entry `linear-api-key`.
